context:
Goal: the red-main check never says green while main is red, and never blocks merges while main is green.
Problem (rule): you picked c on item 781: measure first. The number is in. Main skips its full test run after a green PR run of the same code (your ruling own-769), and a skipped run proves nothing, so the red-main check must look back to a run that really ran the tests. Option a judges only runs that ran the tests; b is a plus a full test run on main when the judged run is old. Only you can pick; PR #3297 waits on it.
The number (30 days, 302 pushes to main, 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-14): only 2 of 302 push runs were skipped. Loose reading (the checks or gates job ran): the newest run that ran tests was 0 commits back for 290, 1 back for 6, 2 or more back for 6 (most 5). Strict reading (also every non-Mac test shard ran, 298 counted): 0 back for 183, 1 back for 20, 2 or more back for 95 (90th percentile 49, worst 79), mostly cancelled Windows shards in the newer gates era. Today's head: the newest finished test run was 2.57 hours old at push.
Based on (measure): a read-only Explore agent's read of the REST runs list, relayed by the coordinator 23:10 CST; not re-run by triage. Your pick c on item 781 (19:42 CST), ruling own-781-c-measure-first.
Unknown: what each shard covers; whether skipped Mac jobs are by design; 10 runs had a second attempt and only the last was read.
Departs from: main's red-main check — the 16:06 CST wording on step red-gate-reads-suite-run and the cover signal; a drops the cover, b drops it and adds a full run on main when the judged run is old. Your ruling own-769 (the skip itself) stays.
Meanwhile: PR #3297 waits on this pick.

lastAnswer: 812: a, judge only runs that ran the tests (23:38 CST Nov 13).

options.gain: A red main can never read green by mistake; no extra reads; skips are rare, so it costs little.
options.label: Judge only runs that ran the tests (recommended by the coordinator)
options.lose: A docs-only fix of a red main stays red until a code push goes green, or someone uses --base-red-ok.

options.gain: The judged run is never stale.
options.label: Same as a, plus a full test run on main when the judged run is old
options.lose: An extra full run on main each time, so more CI minutes and Mac spend, for a case the measure shows is rare.

short: Red-main check: judge only test-running runs, or add a full run?
title: Now that the measure is in, should the red-main check judge only runs that ran the tests (a), or also add a full run on main when that run is old (b)?
